text:
The power spec is the only failure. Gain, bandwidth, and offset all pass, so the fault most likely sits in the bias network that sets the total quiescent current. Gain and bandwidth are set by the diff pair, load, and Rz/Cc, and they still look correct.

Tail device M5 is the strongest suspect. It is a 2.02/0.15 nfet mirrored from the 0.49/2.34 reference M6, which gives a current ratio of about 64. That ratio sets almost all of the supply current, and an oversized M5 width would push power up by roughly the observed 2.35x. M6, the reference device, is second because its sizing also sets every mirrored current. M8, the output sink, is third because it adds a smaller bias-set current.

```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "M8"], "fault": "Tail current mirror M5 (oa_t sink) is oversized relative to the reference M6 (W/L ratio ~64x vs. the design value), roughly doubling the tail bias current and pushing total power to ~422 uW, above the 180 uW limit. Restoring M5 to its nominal width should bring power back under spec."}
```
